title: Domitian
lead: Vespasian's younger son, emperor from 14 September AD 81 until he was murdered on 18 September 96. Tacitus says Domitian took his career further (Histories of Tacitus 1:1).

sections.b:
Wikipedia lists Tacitus as praetor in 88 under Domitian. It notes that Tacitus, Pliny the Younger and Suetonius, writing after Domitian's death, made him out a cruel and paranoid tyrant, and records a historian, Brian Jones, who argues that the bias of the sources makes his real character hard to judge. In AD 69 Domitian was in Rome; he got away from the Capitol in disguise, and once Vitellius was dead on 20 December he came forward and was hailed as Caesar.

Suetonius says Domitian was slain on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of October, 18 September 96 (Domitian 17.3).
